summary: Dr. Douglas Kerr, a neurologist at Johns Hopkins University, led a research team that identified enough chemicals necessary to regrow motor neurons and succeeded in partially restoring paralyzed rats' ability to walk. The results represent major progress toward curing nerve-related problems in humans, such as Lou Gehrig's disease and spinal cord injuries, though Dr. Karr emphasized it will be many years before any possible treatments for humans become available. Dr. Naomi Keitman of the National Institutes of Health's neurology division said, "They did something that people have been trying to do for at least 30 years and literally hit a brick wall until now," and the research will be published in the Annals of Neurology.
